source.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Arthur Conmy; Augustine N. Mavor-Parker; Aengus Lynch; S. Heimersheim; Adrià Garriga-Alonso

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies automated activation-patching circuit discovery to GPT-2 Small IOI and evaluates recovered subgraphs against the previously reported IOI circuit. It tests the same circuit-recovery question, but uses an automated method and recovery metrics rather than simply reproducing the original manual analysis.
record.gate_note: The IOI experiment uses 50 examples from one template and an ABC corrupted dataset. The paper also reports comparisons across recovery algorithms, activation corruptions, and optimization metrics. Results for other tasks, referenced findings from other studies, and values used only to choose parameters are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Automated circuit discovery (ACDC, plus adapted SP and HISP) is run on GPT-2 Small IOI and scored against the Wang et al. circuit. Recovery is compared across methods, corrupted vs zero ablation, and KL vs logit-difference objectives. This bears directly on V4 and V5, and partly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add that ACDC with KL and corrupted activations recovers most of the IOI circuit; its main-threshold heads were all in the circuit, with no false positives. However, ACDC and SP miss negative name mover heads, and performance is very sensitive to metric, ablation and hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching on the same GPT-2 Small IOI task and compares against the original circuit, but automates edge removal with ACDC and evaluates recovery using KL divergence, task-specific metrics, and ROC curves. It also varies corrupted versus zero activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The IOI recovery results vary with activation replacement (corrupted versus zero), objective metric (KL versus IOI logit difference), recovery threshold, and edge-level versus node-level evaluation. The study uses one IOI template and does not test prompt-distribution sensitivity.
record.problems: The IOI experiment uses N=50 examples from one template. Recovery is evaluated against a human-reported canonical circuit that the paper says may contain extraneous edges or miss important edges. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these IOI comparisons and notes that results are sensitive to design choices. Its description of the head classes found in Figure 1 is inconsistent between Appendix F.2 and F.3.
record.rows_left_out: None; all extracted IOI-specific results fit within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: The full faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests of the original are not rerun; only circuit vs model logit difference/KL and the overlap of ACDC's heads with the circuit.
Backup name-mover self-repair is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse are not tested for IOI.
Sensitivity to prompt distribution is not tested: one template, N=50.
Name orders, other templates and more names are not tested.

missing.what: ROC curves for IOI using Abs Logit Diff vs Logit Diff vs KL objectives; the authors say Abs Logit Diff is worse than both (no AUC given).
Under a performance-matching objective, a subgraph's IOI logit difference swung between 5.0 and 1.5 within one ACDC run (instability, order dependence).
Optimizing logit difference produced IOI subgraphs with logit difference over 15, well above the model's (over-optimization).
The canonical IOI circuit used for ROC labels was reimplemented at the level of Q/K/V and MLPs, with 1041 edges; the reimplementation itself is a choice that affects scores.

record.verdict_notes: The study's own method (ACDC) is compared against SP and HISP. These rows are kept because method agreement on the IOI circuit is exactly what V4 asks, but the authors frame them as method benchmarks. They also say the canonical circuit is unreliable ground truth, limiting the AUC conclusions. No uncertainty is reported, and the prompts are N=50 from a single template. The values for the circuit's logit difference are inconsistent: 3.24 in F.2 vs 3.55 in C.3.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not independently test all of the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a complete set; its main ACDC run recovers only a subset of the proposed circuit.
Whether backup heads take over after main name-mover heads are ablated.
Whether the same circuit classes and roles occur in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks, or are reused for other tasks.
The study compares ACDC with SP and HISP and varies activation corruption and metric, but does not establish exact circuit equivalence across methods or test other circuit-finding methods.

The study varies recovery method, ablation type, and metric, and reports a gap between the canonical circuit and the full model's logit difference. It uses one IOI template, so it does not test sensitivity to different IOI prompt distributions.
Other name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied ACDC to recover an IOI subgraph at threshold τ = 0.0575.

conditions.value: N=50 examples from one IOI template
heads not split into query, key, and value

rows.measure: Recovered heads and their relation to the canonical IOI circuit
rows.baseline: Canonical circuit has 26 heads; paper text gives 144 total GPT-2 Small heads
rows.value: 9 heads; all are in the canonical IOI circuit; the paper says they include three head classes and suffice to complete IOI
rows.note: The text is inconsistent about which classes appear in this result: F.2 names Previous Token, S-Inhibition, and Name Mover heads, while F.3 says the Figure 1 circuit omits Previous Token heads.
rows.check: ACDC selected 9 heads, all inside the 26-head circuit, with no false positives; this bears on V4 as well as V1. Not all classes were found: no Negative Name Movers. The text conflicts on Previous Token heads (F.2 says included, F.3 says not).

source_check.locator_found: Figure 1; Appendix C opening; Appendix F.1–F.3.

conditions.value: canonical IOI circuit from Wang et al. (2023)

rows.measure: Logit difference
rows.baseline: Full model: 4.11
rows.note: The paper also reports KL divergence of 0.44 between the canonical circuit and the original model.
rows.check: Canonical circuit logit difference is 3.24 vs 4.11 for the model (~79%), under ABC resample ablation on one template. Appendix C.3 instead says the IOI circuit has logit difference 3.55; the discrepancy is unexplained.

source_check.correct: V1: partial. V5: observed for the clause that the circuit explains only part of the behaviour. Appendix F.2 gives circuit 3.24 and model 4.11.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix F.2, final paragraph; Appendix C.3.
source_check.problem: Partial faithfulness supports V5's partial-explanation clause; the state should differ by version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Ran ACDC at a lower threshold while optimizing KL divergence.
rows.measure: Recovered edges and head types
rows.baseline: Full computational graph has 32923 edges
rows.value: 443/32923 edges; includes Negative Name Mover heads, and also heads not documented in the IOI circuit
rows.note: The lower threshold recovers some additional reported components but also produces extraneous heads.
rows.check: This is a method-recovery result, not a test of the circuit itself; relink it from V1 to V4/V5. Negative Name Movers were recovered only at a very low threshold (443 edges), together with undocumented heads (9.2, 11.11).

source_check.correct: V4: partial. V5: observed through the threshold and objective comparisons. Figure 15 reports 443/32923 edges at τ=0.00398, including negative heads and additional heads.
source_check.problem: Incomplete canonical recovery and observed evaluation sensitivity require different version-specific states.

rows.check: Relink from V1 to V4/V5: this is about method recovery. Negative Name Movers were never recovered with the logit-difference objective; for V5 this shows metric dependence (observed).
